blocks.text: Zscaler provides a number of ways to provision users, groups, and departments as described in About Provisioning and Authentication Methods. This article describes how to manage user accounts on the Users page as well as provides an overview of its features. You can add up to 1400K users. For a complete list of ranges and limits per feature, see Ranges & Limitations.
Users provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Manage users within your organization who have access to the Internet & SaaS service.
View users enrolled for the Internet & SaaS service.

blocks.text: If you select Active Directory or OpenLDAP when configuring the default authentication profile, or if your organization uses Authentication Service for Admins, users are listed as view only with limited options (i.e., download user data and search for users). If your organization uses Authentication Service for Admins and Users, users are configured with Authentication Service. To learn more, see About Users.

blocks.heading: About the Internet & SaaS Users Page

blocks.text: On the Internet & SaaS Users page (Administration > Internet & SaaS Authentication > Internet & SaaS Users > Users), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Search for a configured user.
Download a CSV file that lists your users.
Select which columns are visible in the table.
Enable or disable filtering for the table.
Filter the table by user ID, name, group, or department.
View a list of configured users. For each user, you can see the following information:
User ID or Name: The user's username or domain name.
Display Name : The user's display name that is visible throughout the Zscaler Admin Console when configuring policies.
Groups: The groups the user belongs to.
Department: The department the user belongs to.
Status: The status of the user.

User Risk Profile: Displays the User Risk Score that is generated based on DLP violations, risky user behavior, unsanctioned cloud application usage, and other suspicious factors. If the score is higher than Low, you can click the Reset icon next to the score to reset it to Low. To learn more, see About the User Risk Report.
This column only appears if you select Enable Real-Time Risk Score Updates in the Advanced Settings.
Comments: Comments regarding the user, if available.
Edit a configured user.
Reset the user's risk score.
Go to the Groups page.
View a list of predefined groups created by the Zscaler service.
Go to the Departments page.
